about: Concept graph of the Django track: what each concept needs first (requires; python:<id> is a concept of the Python track), what it lets you do (can), its lesson and its exercises.

concepts.name: HTTP in one page
concepts.can: Can explain a request and a response (method, path, headers, body, status), safe and idempotent methods, and the common status codes

concepts.name: Project and app layout
concepts.can: Can create a project and an app, say what manage.py, settings.py, urls.py and INSTALLED_APPS each do, and run the development server

concepts.name: The request cycle
concepts.can: Can trace a request from the server through middleware and the URLconf to a view and back, naming each step

concepts.name: URL routing
concepts.can: Can write path() routes with converters and names, include() other URLconfs, and build URLs with reverse() instead of hand-writing them

concepts.name: Function views
concepts.can: Can write a view that reads the request, returns the right response (HTML, JSON, redirect, 404) and restricts the HTTP methods

concepts.name: Middleware
concepts.can: Can write a middleware class, say why the order in MIDDLEWARE matters, and name what runs on the way in and on the way out

concepts.name: Templates
concepts.can: Can render a template with context, use tags, filters and template inheritance, and explain automatic escaping

concepts.name: Static and media files
concepts.can: Can explain STATIC_URL, collectstatic and why user uploads (media) are different from static files

concepts.name: Relational databases in one page
concepts.can: Can explain tables, rows, primary and foreign keys, joins, indexes and why a database enforces constraints

concepts.name: Models and fields
concepts.can: Can define a model with typed fields, constraints, default ordering and methods, and say what SQL table it becomes

concepts.name: Relationships
concepts.can: Can model one-to-many, many-to-many and one-to-one relations, choose on_delete deliberately, and use related_name

concepts.name: The migration workflow
concepts.can: Can use makemigrations, migrate, showmigrations and sqlmigrate, read a migration file, resolve two leaf migrations after a merge, and say when to squash

concepts.name: Data migrations
concepts.can: Can write a RunPython step with the historical models (apps.get_model), make it reversible and cheap on a big table, and know when RunSQL is the right tool

concepts.name: The admin site
concepts.can: Can register models, configure list_display, search, filters and inlines, and say what the admin should and should not be used for

concepts.name: QuerySets
concepts.can: Can explain that QuerySets are lazy and cached, chain filter and exclude, use get, order, slice and count, and say when the database is actually hit

concepts.name: Lookups, Q and F
concepts.can: Can use field lookups across relations, combine conditions with Q, and use F expressions to compare or update fields in the database

concepts.name: Aggregation
concepts.can: Can use aggregate and annotate (Count, Sum, Avg), filter on annotations, and group with values()

concepts.name: Following relations
concepts.can: Can reach related objects forwards and backwards, and use select_related to fetch a row and its related row in one query

concepts.name: Bulk operations
concepts.can: Can use update, delete, bulk_create, bulk_update, get_or_create and update_or_create, and say what each skips (save, signals)

concepts.name: Transactions and locking
concepts.can: Can use atomic blocks and savepoints, select_for_update, and on_commit, and explain what autocommit means and what a rollback undoes

concepts.name: Raw SQL and EXPLAIN
concepts.can: Can drop to raw() or a cursor safely (parameters, never string formatting) and read an EXPLAIN plan at a basic level

concepts.name: Forms and validation
concepts.can: Can define a Form with field and cross-field validation (clean_<field>, clean), show errors and render it safely

concepts.name: Model forms
concepts.can: Can use a ModelForm, save(commit=False), and explain why form validation and database constraints are both needed

concepts.name: POST, redirect, messages
concepts.can: Can handle a POST, redirect after success (post/redirect/get), show a one-time message, and explain why the CSRF token is there

concepts.name: Class-based views
concepts.can: Can write a View subclass, say how dispatch picks a method, and use mixins without losing track of the call order

concepts.name: Generic views
concepts.can: Can use ListView, DetailView, CreateView, UpdateView and DeleteView, override get_queryset, and paginate

concepts.name: Authentication flow
concepts.can: Can use login and logout, authenticate(), login_required and a login-required middleware, and explain what an authentication backend does

concepts.name: A custom user model
concepts.can: Can say why AUTH_USER_MODEL should be set before the first migration, choose between AbstractUser and AbstractBaseUser, and keep profile data separate

concepts.name: Permissions and groups
concepts.can: Can use model permissions, groups and has_perm, protect views with mixins or decorators, and say what object-level permission needs beyond the default

concepts.name: Sessions
concepts.can: Can compare database, cache and signed-cookie session engines, set expiry, and explain session fixation and why login rotates the key

concepts.name: Web security basics
concepts.can: Can explain and prevent XSS, CSRF, SQL injection and clickjacking in Django, and name the settings for HTTPS cookies, HSTS, host validation and a content security policy

concepts.name: Login limits and lockout
concepts.can: Can design limits on failed logins (per account and per address), and say what a lockout can be abused for

concepts.name: TestCase and the test client
concepts.can: Can write Django tests with TestCase, the test client and RequestFactory, and assert on status, content, redirects and templates

concepts.name: pytest-django
concepts.can: Can use pytest-django (the django_db mark, client, settings and urls fixtures) and build test data with fixtures or factories

concepts.name: Query-count tests
concepts.can: Can assert the number of queries a view or function makes and use it to catch an N+1 regression

concepts.name: Testing forms and models
concepts.can: Can test validation, constraints and model methods, including the database-level rules

concepts.name: Isolation and slow things
concepts.can: Can explain that each test runs in a transaction, when TransactionTestCase is needed, and how to isolate time, settings and outside services

concepts.name: The N+1 problem
concepts.can: Can spot an N+1 in code and in the query log, fix it with select_related or prefetch_related (and Prefetch with a custom queryset), and explain the fetch modes added in Django 6.1

concepts.name: Database indexes
concepts.can: Can add single, composite and partial indexes, say what an index costs on writes, and check with EXPLAIN that a query uses it

concepts.name: Caching
concepts.can: Can use per-view, template-fragment and low-level caching with Redis, and design key naming, timeouts and invalidation

concepts.name: Pagination and large result sets
concepts.can: Can paginate with Paginator, explain why large offsets are slow and what keyset pagination does, and use iterator() for big loops

concepts.name: Precomputed rollups
concepts.can: Can decide when to store a precomputed summary instead of aggregating on every request, and design its refresh and correction

concepts.name: Measure first
concepts.can: Can profile a slow page with a debug toolbar, the query log and timing, and follow the rule of measuring before optimising

concepts.name: REST in one page
concepts.can: Can explain resources, methods, status codes, idempotency and statelessness, and how REST differs from RPC, GraphQL and webhooks

concepts.name: Serializers
concepts.can: Can write Serializer and ModelSerializer classes with validation, nested and read-only fields, and explain input versus output shape

concepts.name: API views, viewsets and routers
concepts.can: Can write APIView, generic views and ViewSets, register routers, and choose between them

concepts.name: API authentication and permissions
concepts.can: Can use token and session authentication and permission classes, and apply throttling

concepts.name: Filtering, searching, pagination
concepts.can: Can add filtering (django-filter), search, ordering and pagination, and say what each costs the database

concepts.name: Errors and versioning
concepts.can: Can return consistent errors with the right status codes, and version an API without breaking clients

concepts.name: OpenAPI documentation
concepts.can: Can generate an OpenAPI schema (for example with drf-spectacular), serve interactive docs, and treat the schema as the contract

concepts.name: Testing an API
concepts.can: Can test an API with APIClient, authenticated and anonymous, including validation errors and permissions

concepts.name: App boundaries
concepts.can: Can split a project into cohesive apps, avoid circular imports between them, and say what belongs in which app

concepts.name: Settings per environment
concepts.can: Can organise base, development, test and production settings, read configuration from the environment, and keep secrets out of the repository

concepts.name: Services and selectors
concepts.can: Can keep views and serializers thin by putting business logic in service functions and reads in selectors, and explain the trade-off

concepts.name: Managers and custom QuerySets
concepts.can: Can write reusable query logic as QuerySet methods and a manager, and chain them

concepts.name: Signals and their risks
concepts.can: Can use signals and say why hidden coupling makes them risky, and when a service call or on_commit is clearer

concepts.name: Management commands
concepts.can: Can write an idempotent management command with arguments and decide between a command, a scheduled task and a one-off script

concepts.name: Feature flags
concepts.can: Can use flags, switches and samples (for example django-waffle) to ship dark, roll out gradually and remove the flag afterwards

concepts.name: Audit trails
concepts.can: Can record who did what and when, including read access, and design retention and tamper-resistance

concepts.name: Error handling and reporting
concepts.can: Can turn domain exceptions into the right HTTP responses, log errors with context, and report them

concepts.name: WSGI, ASGI and the event loop
concepts.can: Can explain the difference between WSGI and ASGI, what an event loop does, and why async helps for waiting but not for computing

concepts.name: Async views and the async ORM
concepts.can: Can write an async view, use the async ORM methods, call sync code with sync_to_async, and avoid blocking the event loop

concepts.name: Channels consumers and routing
concepts.can: Can write a WebSocket consumer, route it, and join and leave groups

concepts.name: Channel layers
concepts.can: Can configure a Redis channel layer, send to a group from a view or a task, and explain message expiry and what happens when a consumer is slow

concepts.name: WebSocket authentication
concepts.can: Can authenticate a WebSocket with the session or a token, validate the origin, and reject unauthorised connections

concepts.name: Polling, long polling, SSE, WebSockets
concepts.can: Can choose between polling, long polling, server-sent events and WebSockets for a given need

concepts.name: Celery tasks with Django
concepts.can: Can set up Celery with Django, write shared tasks, pass only serialisable arguments, and run a worker

concepts.name: Retries and idempotency
concepts.can: Can add retries with backoff, time limits and late acknowledgement, and make a task safe to run twice

concepts.name: Enqueue after commit
concepts.can: Can explain the race between a task and an open transaction and fix it with on_commit

concepts.name: Scheduled tasks
concepts.can: Can schedule periodic tasks with Celery beat (including the database scheduler), and handle time zones and missed runs

concepts.name: The outbox pattern
concepts.can: Can store work in the database first and let a message carry only an id, and say why the database, not the broker, is the source of truth

concepts.name: Queues and workers
concepts.can: Can route tasks to queues, set concurrency, prefetch and memory limits, and say what each protects against

concepts.name: Django's built-in Tasks
concepts.can: Can describe the Tasks framework added in Django 6.0 (definition and queueing in Django, running by an external worker) and compare it with Celery

concepts.name: Monitoring tasks
concepts.can: Can detect failed, stuck and piling-up tasks, expire results, and add health checks

concepts.name: A Compose stack
concepts.can: Can describe and run a stack of web, worker, scheduler, database and cache containers with Compose, with health checks, networks and volumes

concepts.name: Application servers
concepts.can: Can choose and configure an application server (gunicorn, uvicorn or daphne), its worker count and timeouts

concepts.name: Reverse proxy and HTTPS
concepts.can: Can put a reverse proxy in front, terminate TLS, forward the right headers, and set the proxy-related settings so Django knows the request was HTTPS

concepts.name: Serving static and media in production
concepts.can: Can serve static files (collectstatic, WhiteNoise or a proxy) and media (object storage) and use the STORAGES setting

concepts.name: Migrations in a release
concepts.can: Can run migrations on deploy, write backwards-compatible migrations, and plan a rollback

concepts.name: Backup and restore
concepts.can: Can back up PostgreSQL, encrypt and rotate backups, and run a restore drill that proves they work

concepts.name: Logging and monitoring
concepts.can: Can configure LOGGING, write structured logs, expose a health endpoint and watch the key metrics

concepts.name: Secrets and configuration
concepts.can: Can keep secrets out of images and the repository, load them at run time and rotate them

concepts.name: Upgrading Django
concepts.can: Can plan an upgrade between releases (LTS to LTS), read release notes and deprecation warnings, and use the test suite as the safety net

concepts.name: Deploying to a cloud account
concepts.can: Can deploy the stack to a real cloud account, with a cost estimate, secrets handled, a rollback plan and a teardown
